# Anatomy of the Ark

*Pages PDF 20-24*

## **Anatomy of the Ark**
_Temple of Spite_ is an immense labyrinth of stone, a city unto itself, filled with countless halls, winding staircases, and shadowed corridors. It is ancient and oppressive, with the original fortress of Athil Khairn intact at the heart of newer constructions that loom over flagged courtyards and decks. 

The black ark is roughly the shape of a colossal ship, with a sharp prow and long rocky walls rising above the waves. Vertically, it is unfeasibly tall, a soaring structure that reflects its origins as a sorcerer’s spire in ancient Nagarythe, and the towers of _Temple of Spite_ rest on the same bedrock that once supported Athil Khairn. In many places, this dark, almost black, granite is worked into the structure of the buildings that rise from the ark’s decks, while jagged spurs and outcrops of stone surround the walls along the waterline. 

Above the exposed rocks, the ark’s sides resemble city ramparts, studded with watchtowers, ornate buttresses, and battlements guarded with repeater bolt throwers positioned to attack enemy craft. In cases of enemy boarding action, or mutiny among the crew, the bolt throwers can be pivoted inwards to aim at targets on the deck of the ark. 

## **A Floating Citadel**
The architecture is a twisted mirror of high elf styles, incorporating slim spires ringed with elegant, tapering spines. Each construction on _Temple of Spite_ is carefully fashioned and situated to manipulate the dark magic flowing around the black ark. Whereas concentrations of _Dhar_ tend to pool and stagnate, the architecture stirs up the magic to weave patterns and eddies that keep _Temple of Spite_ afloat and alleviate the effects of dark yenlui on the inhabitants. Much like the aestheticists of Ulthuan, the architects position structures, shrines, and ornamentation for reasons beyond mere appearance. 

Amongst the towers are four lofty masts, each the height of Naggaroth’s tallest pines, which hold vast lateen sails, to supplement the magical impetus of the black ark by harnessing mundane winds. _Temple of Spite_ stays afloat and moves by channelling magic around and through its bulk, sustained by sacrifices and three mystical nexuses distributed through the ark. These are protected by elite guards chosen by the fleetmaster and supreme sorceress, as they are the only elves who are permitted to approach each nexus. If these structures are compromised, the delicate weave of dark sorcery will unravel, and the ark will sink like the immense stone citadel it is. 

There are three main clusters of towers and buildings above the waterline: the Vanguard Spires stand at the fore of the vessel, the domain of the sorceresses; the Fleetmaster’s Bastion is a citadel, and headquarters of the ark’s command; and the temple of Khaine presides over Valeth’s Palace at the aft of the ark. 

Shadowed passageways and stone walkways weave between the towers, allowing passage along the decks. The light of the sun rarely reaches these tight alleyways, so they are lined with sconces containing magical witchlights that lend them an eerie luminescence. Within the larger buildings and below the surface, a labyrinth of servants’ tunnels allows the lowliest inhabitants of the ark to move around out of sight of their social betters. 

## **A Troubling Fissure**
Eleven years ago, a hairline crack appeared in a tunnel between the Fleetmaster’s Bastion and Valeth’s Palace. What began as a tiny fracture now oozes brine. Everyone is too scared to tell the Black Convocation, for while the damage is clearly troubling, bearers of bad news tend to meet a horrific end. Lady Hawkbane’s underlings need someone to discover it and tell the castellan, who will then tell Helbane. Whatever happens, they want to make it someone else’s responsibility. 

## **Vanguard Spires**
Looming behind the huge, banked prow are the Vanguard Spires, lashed by spray and wreathed in sorcerous mists. 

## **The Stalkers’ Spire**
The foremost tower on _Temple of Spite_ , the Stalkers’ Spire is frequented by corsairs taking the fore watch and those charged with seeking prey for the vessel. It houses a temple of Anath Raema, symbolically positioned as eager to pursue the ark’s quarry. Corsairs and beastmasters visit to offer thanks to the goddess of the savage hunt and petition for a keen eye and strong arm. Within the spire, the walls are bedecked with skins and heads taken from quarry hunted in the name of Anath Raema. 

## **The Mistborne Vigil**
This watch tower dominates the Spires. It houses a coven of sorceresses, overseen by Supreme Sorceress Xalthea from opulent chambers halfway up the tower. The interior walls are panelled with black marble, shot through with veins of amethyst and glacial blue and carved with elven runes, each playing a role in manipulating the flow of magic through the tower and the ark. 

The Temple of SpiTe 

The upper chambers contain a wide pillared hall where the sorceresses perform rituals to serve the ark. When the ark is propelled by sorcery alone, the sorceresses assemble here to channel the stream of _Dhar_ required for propulsion. The members of the coven dwell on the lower levels, their chambers designed to reflect their individual aesthetics and interests, and they keep a shared library of scrolls and grimoires. The blackpine door that leads to this room is bound with complex sorceries to keep all but the sorceresses out. 

Below the Mistborne Vigil is a chamber for one of the fabled tainted stones. Aeons past, the high elves created crystalline artefacts to aid ships exploring the world, and several of these crystals were acquired by dark elves and warped to serve their purposes. The tainted stone Khaith’ssar is one of the three sorcerous nexuses that keep the ark afloat; it refines _Dhar_ to counter the bulk of the vessel, allowing it to cut through the waves with unexpected swiftness. 

## **The Moon Spire**
A slender tower rising behind the Mistborne Vigil, the Moon Spire takes its name from the shrine to Lileath at its summit. Sorceresses and corsair captains use the moons to navigate and this modest shrine is where they invoke the moon goddess for guidance at sea. The tower is cold and few dwell there long, as those who sleep in the tower may experience disturbing prophetic dreams. If Mannslieb is full, anyone sleeping here overnight gains two Fortune Points (which they may keep until Mannslieb is next full) and the _Doomed_ Talent (if they do not already have one). 

## **Venomblade Hall**
Located at the base of the Vanguard Spires is a barracks housing dark elf soldiers under the command of Selentha Ebonflame. The soldiers billeted here are notoriously arrogant, even by dark elf standards. A small shrine to Eldrazor is kept adjacent to the Venomblade Hall. 

## **Whispering Walls**
Sorceresses traffic with many dark entities, which leave traces in the stonework of the Vanguard Spires. Helrith Vilethorn cannot identify when he first heard his name muttered from the walls of the Venomblade Hall, but they have promised him greatness. As sleepless nights wear on, his aim with the crossbow improves each day when he takes to the summit of the Moon Spire to pick off unwitting servants. The whispers tell him that he must kill 24 more victims to receive their full gratitude. 

## **Music for the Weary Spirit**
Calimir moonbough is one of the most valuable possessions on the black ark. The high elf is a poet from Tiranoc, composer of exquisite elegiac verse that laments the passing of the elves and the lost world of Ulthuan before the Sundering. Druchii highborn crave his performance just as they loathe him for his loyalty to the phoenix king. His recitals are so beautiful and melancholy that they speak to the soul of the Druchii. Calimir has changed hands several times, as highborn scheme to steal him from one another. Those who covet his performances will recruit Characters to kidnap him. Little do the Druchii realise that he plays his masters like his harp, through subtle allusion in his performances he undermines their morale, and he will happily . help any Characters sowing discord on the _Temple of Spite_ 

Polished obsidian and marble from Ulthuan form smooth, flowing arches and darkly-beautiful carvings, retaining the architecture and rare beauty of the original elven halls, albeit decorated with the macabre artwork of the Druchii. Below the fleetmaster’s rooms are several large chambers, which serve as ballrooms, places of assembly, and dining halls. Helbane’s gallery can also be found here, housing his collection of plundered trophies and artworks. 

## **The Nexus Sanctum**
A permanent guard of elite soldiers armed with repeater crossbows stands outside a bolted door halfway up the tower. Beyond this barrier, a complex metal apparatus of curved spikes takes up most of the room. This device is the second nexus, a spiked metal apparatus that forms part of the magical network that keeps the black ark afloat. 

## **Seylith’s Fang**
To the fore of the Chain Spire, the Fang is quarters for the warhost’s military commanders, separated from the corsair captains dwelling across the ark. The Fang has a starker appearance than other towers, and the interiors are relatively spartan. Lord Tualarc is commander of the army, his apartments are stark and austere, adorned only with the bare necessities, each of his possessions meticulously placed. 

## **Aelrath-Kar**
## **Fleetmaster’s Bastion**
Amidships is the Fleetmaster’s Bastion, the dominant citadel on the ark where Duriath Helbane presides over _Temple of Spite_ and its fleet. These buildings are formed about the original keep of Athil Khairn, extended over the centuries since the Sundering with additional towers, halls, bridges, and a complex of smaller keeps and walled enclosures. 

## **The Chain Spire**
The Chain Spire looms high over the whole ark, the seat of Helbane’s power. This is almost a fortress in itself, where the most exalted elves on _Temple of Spite_ dwell in opulent quarters. The higher in the ark’s social hierarchy, the more elevated their chambers, putting the highborn both literally and figuratively closer to the fleetmaster and his court. These rooms reflect each noble’s personal tastes, as individual as their inhabitants. The summit houses the fleetmaster’s throne room, council chambers, his private apartments, and lodgings for his most trusted servants and advisers. 

This is a complex of smaller towers on the starboard side of the Chain Spire. Successful merchants and high-ranking servants reside here, and these inhabitants are notorious for conspiring to elevate their station on the ark. 

## **The Tower of Trellech**
Many corsairs live here when they are not sailing with the fleet. The tower is sparsely furnished and plainly decorated, having the mood of a space in which no one stays for long. This impersonal feel befits the roaming nature of its inhabitants, and the corsairs may share cabins yet never see one another. A rowdy drinking lodge within the walls makes the tower boisterous at night. 

## **Sylaria’s Lodge and the Tempest Lodge**
These two buildings overlook the sea from the starboard and port sides respectively. Each houses companies of corsairs, including those dedicated to crewing the ark itself, such as the Fell Brethren (see page 76). 

## **Bladesong Hold and Ironbrood Hall**
The interior of the Chain Spire is the most refined on the ark, displaying an elegant symmetry of design and artfully considered aesthetics, the legacy of Athil Khairn. 

These two barracks are built close to the Fleetmaster’s Bastion. These are compact three-storey fortresses housing regiments from the warhost’s infantry. Regimental banners hang from the walls and pennants fly from the battlements. 

The Temple of SpiTe 

## **Temple of Mathlann**
The temple of Mathlann is open to the elements, symbolically exposed to the sea god’s wrath. Most inhabitants of the ark visit the temple to offer captives as sacrifices to Mathlann, for they know that no matter how powerful the ark may be, the fate of the crew is dependent on the whims of the sea god. The walls of the temple are fashioned from the rough stone of the ark, and there is a large statue of Mathlann at the entrance, with a cruel expression defying all who enter to test his wrath. The Druchii storm witch Neryssa Moonwake presides over the temple. 

## **Food Stores and Kitchens**
The lowest levels of the Fleetmaster’s Bastion contain food stores and kitchens reserved for the ark’s most privileged inhabitants. The cooks here are true artisans, who conjure exquisitely decadent dishes for their betters, and the stores are secured and guarded by soldiers of the Spears of the Drowned Moon. The cold store is especially macabre, a magically-chilled forest of hanging carcasses destined for the fleetmaster’s table. 

## **Valeth’s Palace**
Valeth’s Palace is a complex of low towers and halls at the stern of the vessel, each building paying figurative homage to the temple of Khaine raised above them. Other than the temple and great hall, the corridors are more cramped and winding than elsewhere, and more likely to be littered with skulls, bones, or stained with blood. Grisly trophies hang from slender spikes and chains hammered into the walls. 

The less favoured inhabitants of the ark are posted here, along with the most zealous Khainites. Lowborn dark elves live in servants’ chambers throughout the ark, small cells, tightly packed side-by-side along the dark, narrow corridors. 

## **The Colonnade**
The Colonnade is a small, fortified chamber housing the ark’s third nexus behind three barred doors. Tendrils of _Dhar_ are channelled and focused through three glass columns, each carved with sigils and swirling patterns. Several of the sorceresses’ acolytes are posted here to continually focus their magical energy upon the columns, occasionally supervised and chastised by their mistresses. 

## **The Great Hall**
The lower classes who live in Valeth’s Palace gather to eat and socialise in this long, low hall. Gossip and vicious rumours abound, as temporary alliances and betrayals play out amongst the servants and menials. When the Khainites are especially murderous, a tepid solidarity emerges, uniting the inhabitants against the violence such lowly folk are likely to face at such times. 

## **Harpy Aeries**
There are nests for harpies at the summit of Valeth Palace’s towers. Beastmasters keep the harpies fed and goad them to fight, but they are hardly tame, and any vulnerable individual walking the decks of _Temple of Spite_ runs the risk of attack. A more mundane risk arises from the deposits of harpy guano that regularly spatters the decks below Valeth’s Palace. 

## **The Inner Docks**
Below Valeth’s Palace are the ark’s wharves, hidden behind the Kraken’s Gate, an enormous black iron portcullis at the aft of the vessel that is tall enough for a ravenship to enter in full sail. Vessels can shelter within, with berths for up to seven ships and chained cages for helldrakes and other great sea beasts under the control of the ark’s beastmasters. 

## **Ashreaver Hold**
Three dock cranes loom like skeletal sentinels over the aft of the vessel, each wrought from black iron with chains of barbed steel. They are used to haul carcasses on deck for butchery, and gutted whales and other sea beasts lie here, far from most of the ark’s inhabitants and so sparing them from the pungent reek. 

## **The Temple of Khaine**
This elevated hall is surmounted by a tall statue of the BloodyHanded God himself, fashioned from reddish stone. This is the domain of the death hag Kheitalla, her coven of witch elves, and those dark elves who have dedicated their existence to Khaine. Ornamental pools filled with blood line the open hall, leading towards a cauldron heated by a brazier. Here, vast quantities of blood are collected and boiled, suffusing the air with a ruddy haze and sickening stench. 

A barracks where the youngest and most aggressive dark elf soldiers are posted. They often swagger through Valeth’s Palace in packs, looking to challenge or bully those they encounter. 

## **The Depths**
The black ark’s hull descends deep below the waves, and the caverns, corridors, and chambers that lie below sea level are referred to as the depths. The uppermost levels contain workshops of respected trades, several armouries, and food stores. Spiral staircases lead downwards as pristine corridors give way to rough-hewn tunnels where captives and beasts are kept. Deeper still are forgotten chambers and cracks in the stone, the lair of giant rats and nests of spiders, escaped prisoners, and sinister secrets. 

## **Lorithar’s Way**
A winding passage beneath Valeth’s Palace, lined with artisan’s workshops. Dark elves working here aspire to highborn patronage, and the quality of their work is impressive. They make great use of captive labour and try to avoid the more uncouth element amongst their neighbours. 

## **A Buyer’s Market**
The artisans and traders of Lorithar’s Way are as competitive as any dark elves. Kynrael Hesh is a tailor of renown and a fierce competitor of Sarneth Kial, whose robes are currently favoured by the highborn of the Chain Spire. Kynrael made a pact with a minor daemon to outperform Kial’s business, which backfired when he became physically compelled to sew endless garments without rest. Fine robes are now available in abundance, and the upper echelons are not happy that prices have sunk to a level that almost anyone can dress like them. They would look favourably on anyone who discovers the cause of the problem and deals with it. 

## **The Cells**
Just below the waterline, close to the beast pens, are the most wretched dwellings on the ark. A series of dank, low-ceilinged chambers hold imprisoned captives taken in raids. Each cell houses between 20–100 inhabitants chained to a long stone trough running the length of the chamber. 

## **Galleys and Food Stores**
Most food is stored in the depths, with cold stores holding fish and meat linked to the towers above by deep spiral staircases. The galleys are hellish places, thronged with servants and captives scurrying through cramped corridors and kitchens made unbearable through the extreme heat from the ovens and the scant and ineffective ventilation. 

## **The Beast Pens**
_Temple of Spite_ ’s creatures are housed in rough-hewn chambers, where their noxious stench and terrible roaring screams disturb no one of importance. Each level boasts caverns tailored to their inhabitants’ particular needs, so that the deeper a visitor ventures, the stranger the surroundings become, and the stronger the smell of blood and dung grows. Dimly lit cages hold warbeasts and mounts, while larger corral caverns contain cold ones, horses, and warhounds. The high beastmaster and his retinue dwell here with their charges. See page 99 for more details of the menagerie. 

## **The Reservoir**
Rainwater runs from sluices into the ark’s reservoir, a cavern full of water kept clean by magical stones sunk into the rocky walls. The waters are lit from below by pale witchlights and wells from the ark’s decks and towers are sunk into the cavern. 

## **Ceoryn’s Veil**
## **A Ghoulish Infestation**
Life in the captive cells is desperate. With meagre rations and a pervasive fear of what fate awaits them, the prisoners are a community of sorts, and friendships, alliances, and rivalries soon develop between them. In one particular chamber, desperation drove the inmates to cannibalism, and now a small band of ghouls skulk in the dark, still chained and shunned by their fellow captives. 

Beastmaster Rhelian Kinscourge tolerated the ghouls at first, amused by their antics and the fear they inspired in other captives, but now he is losing valuable stock to the creatures and needs to deal with them before the high beastmaster discovers the problem. Kinscourge is considering whether to send in a band of the tougher captives to clear them out. 

## **The Arena**
This enclosed amphitheatre stages entertainment for up to 200 spectators. There are regular and popular gladiatorial contests fought here by dark elf warriors and corsairs willing to pit their skills against beasts or captives. The fleetmaster and his Black Convocation have their own raised podium, away from the rest of the audience. 

Five centuries ago, the sorceress Ceoryn ventured into a flooded complex of tunnels and magically drained them to carve out her own domain. When Ceoryn died, the tunnels were empty until a fleeing dwarf thrall stumbled upon an entrance. Now they provide a refuge for any who escape their fate as a captive. 

## **Shrine of the Wanderer**
Dark elves drawn to Ladrielle, protector of the hidden or lost, somehow always find their way to this concealed shrine, though to those who have not courted her favour, the cavern is almost impossible to find. The shrine is a sharp contrast to the surrounding tunnels, being lined with unblemished white marble. A permanent mist hangs in the air, revealing fleeting glimpses of the goddess’s silver rune, floating without support. 

## **Temple of Slaanesh**
Buried deep below the ark, far from the scrutiny of Duriath Helbane, is a concealed natural cave. It was discovered by pleasure cultists, who have lined the rocky walls with friezes and tapestries decorated with imagery and symbolism conducive to the debauched worship of Slaanesh. On ritual nights, the Slaanesh worshippers amongst _Temple of Spite_ ’s crew gather here to sing the praises of the Prince of Chaos and indulge in euphoric forbidden celebrations.
